questions.question: What is the primary cause of a buffer overflow vulnerability in a program?
options: Failure to check input data size before writing to a fixed-length memory region
Insufficient entropy in the random number generator used for encryption keys
Improperly configured firewall rules allowing access to internal ports
Use of weak administrative passwords on the host operating system
questions.answer: Failure to check input data size before writing to a fixed-length memory region

questions.question: Which specific memory component is the primary target in a classic 'stack smashing' attack?
options: The saved instruction pointer (return address)
The global offset table entries
The heap management metadata
The read-only text segment
questions.answer: The saved instruction pointer (return address)

questions.question: Why must shellcode generally be position-independent code (PIC)?
options: The exact memory address of the target buffer often varies between executions
PIC is required to bypass hardware-based data execution prevention
String-handling functions cannot process code containing absolute addresses
The operating system only allows the execution of PIC in the stack region
questions.answer: The exact memory address of the target buffer often varies between executions

questions.question: What is the purpose of a NOP sled in a buffer overflow exploit?
options: To increase the likelihood that a jump to a guessed address lands in the shellcode
To clear the CPU cache before the malicious instructions are executed
To bypass address space layout randomization by neutralizing the entropy
To ensure that the shellcode does not contain any forbidden NULL bytes
questions.answer: To increase the likelihood that a jump to a guessed address lands in the shellcode

questions.question: Which programming language is naturally resistant to classic buffer overflow attacks due to its design?
options: Java
C
Assembly
questions.answer: Java

questions.question: How does a stack canary protect a program from a buffer overflow?
options: It is a random value checked before a function returns to detect stack corruption
It encrypts the return address stored on the stack to prevent modification
It monitors the system calls made by the process for suspicious activity
It periodically clears the stack memory to remove any injected shellcode
questions.answer: It is a random value checked before a function returns to detect stack corruption

questions.question: What does the NX (No-Execute) bit defense accomplish at the hardware level?
options: It prevents the CPU from executing instructions located in data segments like the stack
It stops the processor from writing data to read-only memory segments
It restricts the set of available system calls a process can invoke
It forces the CPU to check bounds for every array access automatically
questions.answer: It prevents the CPU from executing instructions located in data segments like the stack

questions.question: How does Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) hinder an attacker?
options: It makes it difficult to predict the memory addresses of system libraries and stacks
It changes the binary opcodes of the shellcode during each program execution
It restricts the process to a very small and isolated virtual address space
It prevents the attacker from overwriting the return address on the stack
questions.answer: It makes it difficult to predict the memory addresses of system libraries and stacks

questions.question: Which technique is specifically used to bypass non-executable stack protections (NX/DEP)?
options: Return-to-libc
NOP sledding
Stack canaries
NULL byte injection
questions.answer: Return-to-libc

questions.question: In a heap overflow attack, what is a typical target for the attacker to overwrite?
options: Linked list pointers used by the memory allocator
The saved frame pointer of the current function
The return address stored at the top of the stack
The static global variables in the data segment
questions.answer: Linked list pointers used by the memory allocator

questions.question: Which C library function is considered dangerous because it does not allow a buffer size limit?
options: gets()
fgets()
strncpy()
snprintf()
questions.answer: gets()

questions.question: What is the primary constraint when crafting shellcode for a string-based buffer overflow?
options: It must not contain any NULL (0x00) bytes
It must be exactly 256 bytes in length
It must only use 16-bit x86 instructions
It must be signed by a trusted certificate authority
questions.answer: It must not contain any NULL (0x00) bytes

questions.question: Which defense mechanism involves maintaining a second copy of return addresses in a separate memory area?
options: Shadow stacks
Guard pages
Address space randomization
Stack canaries
questions.answer: Shadow stacks

questions.question: What occurs during a 'replacement stack frame' attack?
options: The attacker overwrites the saved frame pointer to redirect the caller to a fake frame
The attacker replaces the entire executable binary with a malicious version
The compiler inserts extra padding between every local variable on the stack
The operating system swaps the stack and heap segments in virtual memory
questions.answer: The attacker overwrites the saved frame pointer to redirect the caller to a fake frame

questions.question: What is the purpose of placing 'guard pages' in a process's address space?
options: To cause a segmentation fault if an overflow reaches an unmapped memory region
To log all memory access attempts to a secure administrative file
To provide a sandbox where untrusted code can be executed safely
To store the master copy of all stack canaries used by the program
questions.answer: To cause a segmentation fault if an overflow reaches an unmapped memory region

questions.question: A developer replaces strcpy() with strncpy() in their code. What category of defense is this?
options: Compile-time (safe coding practices)
Run-time (address space protection)
Hardware-level (non-executable bits)
Kernel-level (system call filtering)
questions.answer: Compile-time (safe coding practices)

questions.question: Which memory segment typically grows downward toward lower memory addresses?
options: The stack
The heap
The text segment
The global data area
questions.answer: The stack

questions.question: What is a significant limitation of Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR)?
options: It can sometimes be bypassed using information leaks or brute force on 32-bit systems
It requires significant changes to the source code of every protected application
It drastically reduces the execution speed of the program due to memory overhead
It is incompatible with modern hardware-based data execution prevention
questions.answer: It can sometimes be bypassed using information leaks or brute force on 32-bit systems

questions.question: If an attacker overflows a buffer in the global data area, which of the following is a likely target for corruption?
options: A function pointer stored as a global variable
The return address of the main() function
The local variables of a function currently in the stack
The metadata used by the malloc() library on the heap
questions.answer: A function pointer stored as a global variable

questions.question: Which of these is a typical behavior of shellcode once it has successfully gained control?
options: Spawning a shell with the privileges of the vulnerable process
Requesting a password reset for the system administrator account
Encrypting the entire hard drive and demanding a ransom payment
Scanning the local network for other vulnerable web servers
questions.answer: Spawning a shell with the privileges of the vulnerable process
